set.body: Follow-up from bd-01M441B5J02QVWZY929E1YFGFD (smoother now uses StrictMath.exp on the JVM, so x86 and aarch64 JVM scores agree bit for bit). Remaining: (1) Scala.js has no StrictMath; Node 24 Math.exp differs from fdlibm by 1 ulp on 493 of 1M kernel arguments, so JVM and JS density maps agree only within named tolerances. PRD A-9 requires a representative end-to-end pipeline to be bit-identical on JVM and Scala.js: decide whether that designated pipeline crosses the smoother; if so port fdlibm exp (~50 lines) into shared code. (2) math.pow in Bandwidth.rule (Silverman/Scott) and IqrBandwidth (used by FixationEntropy) differs from StrictMath on x86 for 11,925 of n = 2..100,000; not on the SCORES path. (3) KernelExpJvmSuite only detects a revert on x86_64 JVMs: confirm the hosted Linux runner is x86_64 or add an x86 lane.
set.title: Bit-identical transcendental math across JVM and Scala.js (shared fdlibm exp; pow in bandwidth rules)
